newsitem.title: NORWAY: Testing delayed at promising Saga find.
newsitem.headline: Testing delayed at promising Saga find.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Tuesday bad weather had delayed testing on an encouraging hydrocarbon discovery on the Aasgard area in the Haltenbank off mid-Norway.
The company has drilled two wells in block 6406/2 and both have yielded gas and condensate. The prospect was recently registed under the name Kristin.
Saga spokesman Andreas Qvale said bad weather in the Norwegian Sea had prevented production testing of the discovery, which the company had planned to complete in February or early March.
"We are planning to start the test at the weekend and hopefully be finished by April 1," Qvale said.
Under terms of licence 199, Saga must stop drilling activites in the area from April 1 due to environmental grounds. It can restart again in the summer.

The first discovery in the block was announced in March 1996 by the Norwegian Oil Directorate, which said the results from a first appraisal well indicated recoverable reserves of between 70 and 120 million cubic metres of oil equivalent, or 440 to 755 million barrels of oil equivalent.
Both wells were drilled south and southwest of the Smoerbukk field, which makes up part of the Aasgard development together with Smoerbukk South and Midgard prospects.
Aasgard is currently under development and is scheduled to begin pumping condensate on October 1, 1998, with gas exports due to begin October 1, 2000.
